questions.q: AP staff track invoice exceptions in a shared spreadsheet, but invoices and payments live in the ERP. Your PoC drafts exception decisions. Where should its results end up?
options: In the shared spreadsheet, since that is where people work
In a new database built for the PoC
Back in the ERP, the system of record
In the shared mailbox as an email thread
questions.why: Writing anywhere other than the system of record creates a second truth someone must reconcile by hand.

questions.q: A customer's credit limit is one number in the CRM and another in a sales spreadsheet. Which one wins?
options: The CRM, as the system of record for customer data
The spreadsheet, because it is updated more often
Whichever number is higher
Whichever one the sales team prefers
Neither until IT builds a new system
questions.why: The system of record is the official source of truth for that type of data.

questions.q: Exceptions are about 5 percent of invoice volume. A colleague says they are too small to bother with. What is the better view?
options: Agree, focus only on the standard flow
Agree, exceptions belong to IT not operations
Disagree, because exceptions are always the majority of volume
Exceptions are often a small share of volume but a large share of effort
questions.why: Exceptions fall outside the standard flow and go to people, so they often hold most of the effort and cost.

questions.q: You start with a new client next week. What is a good way to learn their main systems before the first meeting?
options: Ask IT for admin access to every system
Read their annual report and a few of their job postings, which often name the systems
Assume they use the same systems as your last client
Wait until week six to avoid looking unprepared
questions.why: Annual reports show what leadership cares about and job postings often name the exact systems.

questions.q: You are writing the Value Proposition Canvas for AP clerks. One draft pain says 'inefficient process'. How should you improve it?
options: Leave it, since general pains cover more cases
Write what actually happens, such as 'waits two days for buyer approval by email'
Move it to the gains section instead
Replace it with a feature the PoC will build
questions.why: Generic pains carry no information; specific ones come from evidence and can be acted on.

questions.q: When should you use the Business Model Canvas rather than the Value Proposition Canvas?
options: BMC for the user group, VPC for the whole company
BMC only for software companies, VPC for everyone else
BMC at the end of the project, VPC at the start
BMC for the client company as a whole, VPC for the specific user group of your PoC
They are interchangeable, pick either
questions.why: The BMC shows which part of the business your work touches; the VPC shows fit for one user group.

questions.q: In a value proposition, when do you have 'fit'?
options: When pain relievers and gain creators match the pains and gains that matter most to the user
When the value map lists more features than the competitor
When every block of the BMC is filled
When the sponsor approves the canvas
When the pains you find most interesting are addressed
questions.why: Fit means your offer answers what the customer profile says matters, not what you find interesting.

questions.q: In a canvas session, how should you present the draft you bring?
options: Present it as final so the session stays short
Hide it and start from a blank canvas
Present every box as a question and let the client correct you out loud
Present only the boxes you are sure about
questions.why: Client corrections are the most valuable output of the session.

questions.q: Your market scan lists three vendors and your custom PoC. What important option is missing?
options: A fourth vendor with the most features
A market sizing estimate
Your preferred cloud provider
Do nothing, the real baseline every option must beat
questions.why: Do nothing is always an option, and often the real competition.

questions.q: A vendor's site says its tool is '98 percent accurate'. How should this go in your scan?
options: As a fact, since it is on the vendor's site
Marked as 'vendor says', separate from what you verified yourself
Left out completely
Averaged with the other vendors' figures
questions.why: Accuracy figures without a test set you can see are claims and should be labelled as such.

questions.q: Why ask the client's IT and procurement teams what they have evaluated before?
options: So you can reuse the old vendor's pricing
Because procurement must approve every interview
Many problems were looked at once and dropped for a reason worth knowing
So you can avoid mentioning products they already own
To find out which vendor IT dislikes
questions.why: Past evaluations reveal constraints, such as a product that could not read supplier emails.

questions.q: A product fits the need well but fails the client's security questionnaire. How should the scan treat it?
options: Not a real option this year
The best option, since features matter most
A good option once the PoC is done
Equal to the other options
questions.why: A good product that fails the security review cannot be used, whatever its features.

questions.q: A sponsor wants to quote 10 percent fewer late fees as a benefit, but nobody has looked at the ledger. How do you treat it?
options: List it as an unquantified benefit until there is data to back a number
Put 10 percent in the total, it is a reasonable guess
Double it to make the case stronger
Drop all quality benefits from the case
questions.why: Only put a number on risk and quality effects when you have a basis; otherwise list them as unquantified.

questions.q: Your PoC saves 200 hours a month across a team of ten. Nobody is leaving and no hiring is planned to change. How should you present this?
options: As cash savings equal to 200 hours of salary
As two headcount cuts
As freed capacity, stating what the team will do with the hours
As zero value, since no cash is saved
questions.why: Hours are not cash unless something changes, such as a vacancy not filled; otherwise they are freed capacity.

questions.q: Where should the loaded cost per hour in your business case come from?
options: Your own estimate of salaries in that industry
Finance
The vendor's pricing page
The average of what users tell you
The LLM provider's cost calculator
questions.why: Loaded cost includes salary, benefits, taxes and overheads, and must be agreed with finance.

questions.q: Halving run cost barely moves payback, but halving minutes saved moves it a lot. What should the PoC measure first?
options: Run cost, by benchmarking LLM prices
Build cost, by tracking developer hours
Volume, by asking managers for estimates
Minutes saved per case, by timing real cases
questions.why: The input that moves the answer most is what the sponsor is really betting on, so measure it first.

questions.q: A client needs exceptions routed to the right buyer. Their ticketing tool already supports routing rules. What is the best path?
options: Build a custom routing service
Buy a new routing product
Configure the ticketing tool they already own
Hire a contractor to route by hand
questions.why: Configuring an owned system is often cheapest and safest, since licences, security approval and support are in place.

questions.q: Two options score almost the same against the agreed criteria. Which should you lean towards?
options: The one with the longest licence term
The one you find most interesting to build
The one with the most features
The one that is easier to reverse
The one IT has never used
questions.why: When scores are close, a reversible choice keeps options open; a small build is easier to undo than a three-year licence.

questions.q: You plan a custom LLM build, but nobody at the client can maintain it after you leave. What does that make it?
options: A liability rather than an asset
An asset, because it fits the need exactly
Fine, since LLM builds need no maintenance
Fine, as long as the code is commented
questions.why: If no one can own and maintain a build, it becomes a liability once the FDE leaves.

questions.q: When should you agree the decision criteria and their weights with the sponsor and IT?
options: After scoring, to check your favourite wins
Before you score any options
Only if IT pushes back
At handover
Never, the FDE decides the weights
questions.why: Agreeing criteria first makes the result their decision, not your preference.
